request.text:
Ah, a battle! Do try to do something worth a verse.
<long pause>
Gather round, gather round, and mind the pointy end.
<long pause>
Every good song has a fight in the middle. Here's ours.
<long pause>
Ha! That'll rhyme with something.
<long pause>
Hm. We'll leave that out of the ballad.
<long pause>
Oh, that's the second verse, right there!
<long pause>
And here the singer pauses, out of respect.
<long pause>
No, no, no. That's not how this one goes!
<long pause>
Oh, this is the sad part, isn't it. I hate the sad part.
<long pause>
Bless you. You'll get a chorus all your own.
<long pause>
Someone's growing into their legend.
<long pause>
And they lived, and the song went on. For now.
<long pause>
There's a last verse to the Song of the Seven. Nobody's sung it in two hundred years. I'll find it.
<long pause>
Sleep now, sleep now, the river is wide, and the fire keeps watch on the other side.
<long pause>
Songs don't burn. That's why I keep them.
<long pause>
Hum along if you know it. Nobody ever knows it.
<long pause>
You'll want to tell this one well, when you're old. I'd start practising.
<long pause>
She's writing him down so the fire can't have him. That's all a song is, really. Writing someone down where nothing can burn them.
<long pause>
So. Mirewood. Did the Court sing for you? Half the Warden songs ended up in those reeds. I can hear my own verses in them.
<long pause>
Ysolde offered me a verse for a memory. I said no. I'm told that makes me the only person who's ever refused a bargain in Mirewood.
<long pause>
It wasn't the last verse anyway. The fey don't have it either. Whoever kept that one never used the fire.
<long pause>
Not here. Ask me again somewhere colder. Some things you only say where your breath shows.
<long pause>
But watch the hooded one by the door. They've been a step ahead of you since the ford, and a step ahead of me for twenty years.
<long pause>
Quickly, before she's offended. Drink half the water. Pour the rest on the sand, for the farms that burned.
<long pause>
That's the point. You give the sand something you can't spare. Then they give you everything they have.
<long pause>
Every note. Well, you mangled the second verse, but only a little.
<long pause>
While you sleep under this cloth, every Scarwalker in the Sunscar will bleed for you.
<long pause>
Break the peace inside this camp, and no Scarwalker will ever speak your names again. Not your children's, either.
